title: Demurrage and Detention Free Time: Waiver Conditions Applied to a Late-Invoice Waiver
content:
## Clause

A late-invoice waiver on a Demurrage and Detention Free Time demurrage line can, as with a dispute credit, be entered only while the record's status reads invoiced. Being itself a waiver entry, it also answers to the conditions that the commercial goodwill waiver rules apply to every waiver entry. All four of the following must be met, each judged from the company's records:

- **Record status.** The free-time record shows invoiced.

- **Quota.** The commercial goodwill waivers the customer has had in the 365 days up to this waiver are still below the product's goodwill quota in number.
- **Window.** Its date lies inside the goodwill request window that the product allows after the invoice date.
- **No goodwill already on the line.** Nothing booked against the line so far is a commercial goodwill waiver.

## Checklist

| Condition | Read from | Met when |
|---|---|---|
| record status | the free-time record | its status is invoiced |
| quota | the customer's goodwill waivers across all records in the trailing 365 days | their number is below the product's quota |
| window | the invoice date of the line and the product's request window | the waiver date is not after the window's last day |
| earlier goodwill | waivers booked against the line | none with the reason commercial goodwill |

## Illustration (hypothetical)

A customer whose product allows two goodwill waivers a year and who has had one in the past 365 days meets the quota; with two it does not.
